samples.summary: CLI exports now exit 0 with silently missing images, contradicting the documented "unreachable image host exits 2" contract
samples.evidence: `exportPdf` sets `onImageError: reportSkippedImage` unconditionally (pdf-export.ts:118), `exportDocx` passes it as the 4th arg (docs/docx-export.ts:41) and `exportPptxCli` passes it too (slides/pptx-export.ts:20). In `collectAndEmbedImages` (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:99-102) and `DocxExporter.collectImages` (docx-exporter.ts:473-478) the reporter converts a per-image failure into a drop. Every failure the CLI image fetcher raises — `SystemError('NETWORK_ERROR', ...)` from `fetchOrThrow`, `httpError(status, 'Image fetch failed: ...')`, the SSRF refusals — is now swallowed: the command writes the output file and returns exit code 0, with only a `console.warn` line on stderr and nothing in the JSON result body. `packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:751-753` still documents the opposite contract ("A transport failure or a non-OK response is classified like every other CLI request … so an unreachable image host exits 2"). For an agent-facing CLI a totally unreachable image host now yields a "successful" export whose content is silently incomplete, with no machine-readable signal (no non-zero exit, no field in the emitted JSON).

samples.summary: The PDF try/catch wraps decoding as well as fetching, so it swallows failures the caller cannot even retry — and diverges from the DOCX path
samples.evidence: In `collectAndEmbedImages` the `try` starts before `fetcher(src)` and extends over `blob.arrayBuffer()`, `embedPng`/`embedJpg` and `embedAsPng` (lines 81-98). So a corrupt payload, or the Node-only `Image format image/gif requires a DOM Canvas to convert` error from `embedAsPng` (line 142-147), is now reported-and-dropped for the CLI instead of raising the previous clear, actionable error. `DocxExporter.collectImages` (docx-exporter.ts:470-483) wraps only `await fetcher(src)`, leaving `deriveExt`/`zip.file` outside — so the same document can hard-fail a DOCX export while silently losing images in a PDF export. If the intent was 'tolerate an unfetchable src', the PDF try should be narrowed to the fetch call the way the DOCX one is.

samples.summary: An upstream body whose `error` object lacks a string `code` now loses its `error.message` text entirely
samples.evidence: `isErrorEnvelope` (line 135-144) requires `typeof error.code === 'string'`. A body such as `{ error: { message: 'Document is a spreadsheet' } }` therefore falls into the throw path, and `upstreamDetail` (line 199-205) only inspects `body.message` — never `body.error.message` — so the reported message collapses to a bare `HTTP <status>`. The code this replaces (`docs content`, `notes content`, `slides content`, and the import/upload paths) printed such a body verbatim on a truthiness test of `body.error`, so the wording reached the user. The `code` tightening is deliberate, but dropping the sibling `error.message` while carefully preserving `body.message` looks unintentional.

samples.summary: `assertNoDotSegments` misses percent-encoded dot segments, so it is weaker than the invariant its docstring claims
samples.evidence: `assertNoDotSegments` compares each segment against the literal `'.'` and `'..'` only (dry-run.ts:47-52). The WHATWG URL parser also resolves `%2e`, `.%2e`, `%2e.` and `%2e%2e` as single/double-dot segments, so a path segment spelled `%2e%2e` passes this guard and the previewed URL still normalizes one level up. Current callers all route ids through `seg()` (which escapes `%`), so no shipped path reaches it — but the docstring advertises the check as "the same refusal `seg()` makes … the invariant it leaves behind", which is exactly the claim a future caller would rely on. The same gap exists in `seg()` itself (packages/core/src/url/index.ts:56), though there `encodeURIComponent` escapes the `%` first.

samples.summary: Dead ternary: `res.ok` is always true inside the `!res.bytes` branch
samples.evidence: The `!res.ok` case returns at line 73-76, so by line 100 `res.ok` is necessarily `true` and `res.ok ? EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR : exitCodeForStatus(res.status)` can only ever yield `EXIT_SYSTEM_ERROR`. Harmless today, but the surviving branch (and the comment above it about "a 404 is the caller's doc id") describes a state this function can no longer be in, which invites a wrong edit later.

samples.summary: `reportSkippedImage` bypasses the module's injectable `warn` seam, its `[wafflebase]` prefix, and `--quiet`
samples.evidence: Every other advisory in this module goes through `warn`/`defaultWarn` (line 693-699), which writes `\`[wafflebase] ...\`` to `process.stderr` and is injectable for tests. `reportSkippedImage` instead calls `console.warn` with no prefix and no seam, and it is a module-level function so `--quiet` cannot gate it. The result is two different stderr formats for advisory output from the same pipeline.

finding.summary: CLI exports now exit 0 with silently missing images, contradicting the documented "unreachable image host exits 2" contract
finding.evidence: `exportPdf` sets `onImageError: reportSkippedImage` unconditionally (pdf-export.ts:118), `exportDocx` passes it as the 4th arg (docs/docx-export.ts:41) and `exportPptxCli` passes it too (slides/pptx-export.ts:20). In `collectAndEmbedImages` (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:99-102) and `DocxExporter.collectImages` (docx-exporter.ts:473-478) the reporter converts a per-image failure into a drop. Every failure the CLI image fetcher raises — `SystemError('NETWORK_ERROR', ...)` from `fetchOrThrow`, `httpError(status, 'Image fetch failed: ...')`, the SSRF refusals — is now swallowed: the command writes the output file and returns exit code 0, with only a `console.warn` line on stderr and nothing in the JSON result body. `packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:751-753` still documents the opposite contract ("A transport failure or a non-OK response is classified like every other CLI request … so an unreachable image host exits 2"). For an agent-facing CLI a totally unreachable image host now yields a "successful" export whose content is silently incomplete, with no machine-readable signal (no non-zero exit, no field in the emitted JSON).

verdict.reason: All the mechanical claims check out: `onImageError: reportSkippedImage` is wired unconditionally on all three CLI export paths (pdf-export.ts:118, docx-export.ts:41, pptx-export.ts:22), the reporter is only a bounded console.warn (image-fetcher.ts:727-730), and the exporters convert a per-image failure into a drop when a reporter is supplied (pdf-image-painter.ts:99-102, docx-exporter.ts:470-478). But this is not a correctness defect: it is the repository's explicitly specified policy. docs/design/cli.md:1573-1593 states "A refusal is **not** fatal to the export — *for the CLI*… Every CLI export path passes `reportSkippedImage`", and even names the exact caveat the reviewer treats as a bug (the catch spanning decode/embed, so undecodable bytes drop quietly). The lessons file (20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-lessons.md:163-183) records the same decision, noting that the opposite policy was itself a regression for `slides export`. What actually remains is (a) one stale JSDoc sentence at image-fetcher.ts:751-753 — the classification it describes still happens; only the "exits 2" conclusion is no longer true for callers that opt into tolerance, a documentation-accuracy issue; and (b) no machine-readable skipped-image field in the JSON envelope — a deliberately deferred product/design gap. Neither is a wrong condition, missing guard, crash, async mistake, resource leak, or unintended data loss, so under this lens's rubric it is out of scope rather than a blocking bug.

finding.summary: `slides export` (PPTX) has no per-image tolerance, so the new SSRF guard turns a previously-working image into a total export failure
finding.evidence: The change deliberately makes a refused/unreachable image an ordinary outcome and patches both docs paths for it (`pdf-image-painter.ts:99-101` catches and reports; `docx-exporter.ts:448-455` records a failed entry). The slides path was not patched: `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209` builds the same guarded `createImageFetcher`, `packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:14` awaits it unguarded, and `exportPptx` calls `await opts.fetchImage(src)` at `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:162` with no try/catch. Any deck whose image `src` names a non-public host that is not the configured server (an internal MinIO/blob host that used to be fetched fine, a stale intranet URL, or a name whose DNS lookup fails) now rejects and the whole `slides export deck.pptx` aborts through `outputError`, where before this change the image was fetched and embedded.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. `exportPptx` wraps `await opts.fetchImage(src)` in a try/catch (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:172-187) and exposes an `onImageError` reporter (index.ts:73-83); on a caught failure it reports and `continue`s, leaving the src out of `srcToMediaPath`, after which `resolveImageRId` returns `null` (index.ts:305-321) and `elementToXml` drops the image element while still serializing the rest of the slide (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/group.ts:62-67). The CLI slides path IS patched: `exportPptxCli` passes `onImageError: reportSkippedImage` (packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:22), and `reportSkippedImage` only `console.warn`s the redacted src and returns (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:727-730). Therefore a refused/unreachable image under the SSRF guard yields a warning plus a partial deck, not a total `slides export` failure via `outputError` (packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:216-221). The finding's core evidence claims ("no try/catch at index.ts:162", "awaits it unguarded at pptx-export.ts:14", "slides path was not patched") are all contradicted by the working tree.

finding.summary: Address-pinning plain-`http:` image fetches sends `Host: <ip>` on Node, breaking name-based virtual hosts that worked before
finding.evidence: `pinnedUrls` (line 396-404) rewrites every `http:` target's hostname to a resolved IP, and `dialOnce` tries to compensate with `headers: { host }` (line 491). The code's own comment at 476-480 states Node's undici drops `host` as a forbidden header name, so the request really arrives as `Host: <ip>`. Any public image served over plain http from a shared/vhosted origin (very common for CDNs and reverse proxies) will now get the wrong site or a 404 instead of the image. Combined with the new silent-drop behaviour in the docx/pdf exporters, the image just disappears from the export with only a `console.warn`. This is a behaviour regression on a path that worked before the change.

verdict.reason: The finding describes code that does not exist in this repository. There is no `pinnedUrls` or `dialOnce` anywhere in the tree (those names appear only in docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-lessons.md:208, which states they belong to a file dropped in the merge with #648). The cited lines are misidentified: image-fetcher.ts:396-404 is the exempt/allowed address filtering in `assertFetchableImageUrl`, and 476-480 is the `INVALID_PROXY` SystemError in `makeProxyAgent`. The only hostname->IP rewrite in the package is image-fetcher.ts:550, which sits inside the proxy-only branch of `planHop`; the direct (no-proxy) path returns early at 524-531 with the URL untouched and pins via the connector-level `lookup` override in `pinnedAgent` (428-450), so a plain-`http:` direct fetch still sends `Host: <name>` and vhosted origins keep working. On the proxied rewrite path the hop is marked `pinnedThroughProxy` (555) and `issue` (797-799) sends it through `rawRequest`/undici `request` with `headers: { host: authority }` (645-661) precisely because WHATWG fetch forbids `Host`, with a single announced fallback to the name at 832-844. The claimed `Host: <ip>` regression on plain-http image fetches therefore has no code behind it.
